method: They study the dynamics of free fermions in the Hatano-Nelson model with open boundaries, varying disorder strength and measuring entanglement entropy, subsystem entanglement, connected correlation, and mutual information.
result: For small disorder, the area-law becomes logarithmic scaling; for larger disorder, it reenters an area-law regime through an entanglement phase transition. At the critical point, entanglement entropy shows universal algebraic scaling. They also demonstrate absence of conformal invariance in the log-law regime and observe similar transitions with periodic boundaries.
conclusion: Disorder induces entanglement phase transitions in non-Hermitian systems with skin effects, enriching the phase diagram and suggesting universal scaling behavior at criticality.

title: Hoare Meets Heisenberg: A Lightweight Logic For Quantum Programs
authors: Aarthi Sundaram, Robert Rand, Kartik Singhal, Youngchan Cho, And Brad Lackey
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2172 (2026).

We show that Gottesman's (1998) semantics for Clifford circuits based on the Heisenberg representation gives rise to a lightweight Hoare-like logic for efficiently characterizing a common subset of quantum programs. Our applications include (i) certifying whether auxiliary qubits can be safely disposed of, (ii) determining if a system is separable across a given bipartition, (iii) checking the transversality of a gate with respect to a given stabilizer code, and (iv) computing post-measurement states for computational basis measurements. Further, this logic is extended to accommodate universal quantum computing by deriving Hoare triples for the [MATH]-gate, multiply-controlled unitaries such as the Toffoli gate, and some gate injection circuits that use associated magic states. A number of interesting results emerge from this logic, including a lower bound on the number of [MATH] gates necessary to perform a multiply-controlled [MATH] gate.

.
tldr: This paper presents a Hoare-like logic for quantum programs using the Heisenberg representation to reason about Clifford circuits and beyond.
motivation: To provide a lightweight and efficient method for verifying properties of quantum programs.
method: It leverages Gottesman's semantics to derive Hoare triples for Clifford circuits and extends to universal quantum computing via T-gates and magic states.
result: The logic enables certification of qubit disposal, separability, transversality, and post-measurement states, and yields a lower bound on T-gate count for multiply-controlled gates.
conclusion: This offers a practical verification framework for quantum programs and insights into quantum circuit optimization.

title: Steady-state Localization From Local Pumping In Center-of-mass-conserving Diffusion
authors: Ivan Tyukin And Farrukh Mukhamedov Farzona Mukhamedova
abstract: Local driving is usually expected to spread activity through a diffusive system. We show that this intuition can fail when motion is constrained. We study a one-dimensional lattice gas on a ring in which particles move only through paired hops that preserve the overall center of mass, while a local source continuously injects adjacent particles and on-site pairs are removed. Contrary to the expectation that steady injection delocalizes activity around the ring, the system self-organizes into a sharply localized active core around the driven bond, where the density away from this core decays rapidly to near zero. We prove an exact steady-state balance that fixes the total number of on-site pairs, independent of system size and hopping rate. Simulations show that once the active core is well separated from the boundaries, its width and peak amplitude collapse under two dimensionless control parameters and become independent of system size. For multiple identical drives, the single-core width predicts when neighboring active patches begin to overlap and the inactive region disappears. The results identify a simple mechanism by which local pumping and constrained motion generate self-localized steady states.
tldr: This paper shows that local pumping in a center-of-mass conserving diffusive lattice gas leads to self-localized steady states, contrary to intuition that activity spreads.
motivation: The authors challenge the expectation that local driving delocalizes activity in diffusive systems, investigating the effect of center-of-mass conservation on steady-state localization.
method: They study a 1D lattice gas on a ring with paired hops preserving center of mass, local injection of adjacent particles, and on-site pair removal. They derive exact balance conditions and perform simulations to analyze steady-state properties.
result: They prove an exact steady-state balance for total on-site pairs, independent of system size and hopping rate, and show collapse of active core width and amplitude under dimensionless parameters. They also predict overlap of multiple driven cores.
conclusion: The results identify a simple mechanism for self-localization in constrained diffusive systems, offering insights into controlling particle distribution via local pumping and conserved motion.

title: Emergent Symmetry-protected Topological Phases Via Polyakov Confinement In Quantum Spin Systems
authors: Shun-Li Yu And Jian-Xin Li Li-Wei He
abstract: A main theme in modern condensed matter physics is the emergence of fractionalized excitations and gauge structures from quantum spin systems. However, understanding how these exotic degrees of freedom reconfine into new phases of matter remains a fundamental challenge. In this work, we demonstrate that Polyakov’s confinement mechanism-a foundation of compact gauge theory-can serve as a dynamical engine to transform a Dirac spin liquid (DSL) into a symmetry-protected topological (SPT) state. Starting with a DSL with spin-dependent gauge fluxes, we show that the single-occupancy constraint inherent to the physical Hilbert space triggers monopole condensation, dynamically confining bulk spinons while preserving gapless edge modes-realizing a spinon analog of the quantum spin Hall effect. Using a large-scale variational Monte Carlo simulation on a triangular antiferromagnet with an additional Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, we provide microscopic evidence for this confined SPT phase, including a characteristic area law for the Wilson loop and vanishing topological entanglement entropy. Furthermore, we identify a measurable spin-pump response under magnetic fields, which directly encodes the Berry curvature of the parent Dirac cones. Our results reveal a previously unexplored pathway to SPT physics, bridging the fields of gauge theory, quantum magnetism, and topological matter.
tldr: This paper uses Polyakov confinement to transform a Dirac spin liquid into a symmetry-protected topological phase, verified via variational Monte Carlo simulations.
motivation: Understanding how fractionalized excitations reconfine into new phases is a fundamental challenge in condensed matter physics.
method: They performed large-scale variational Monte Carlo simulations on a triangular antiferromagnet with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction, analyzing Wilson loop and topological entanglement entropy.
result: The single-occupancy constraint triggers monopole condensation, confining bulk spinons while preserving gapless edge modes, realizing a spinon analog of the quantum spin Hall effect.
conclusion: The work reveals a new pathway to SPT physics bridging gauge theory, quantum magnetism, and topological matter.

title: Tailoring Reflectionless Complex Media For non-Abelian Braiding Of Acoustic Modes
authors: Hongkuan Zhang And Guancong Ma
abstract: Multiple scattering of sound and light can be tailored for diverse applications. Despite the great progress enabled by technologies such as time-reversal propagation and wavefront shaping, the full control of the transmission matrix remains a significant challenge. In this work, we propose a multi-scattering-based approach to design reflectionless complex media with an arbitrary unitary transmission matrix. As such, the perfect transmission of waves through such a medium performs a unitary operation. Based on this principle, we experimentally demonstrated braiding of multiple waveguide modes in an acoustic waveguide via multiple scattering and showed non-Abelian characteristics arising from the concatenation of distinct complex media. Furthermore, we show that the principle can be extended for realizing arbitrary unitary operations beyond braiding. Our scheme uses generalized Wigner–Smith operators to design the optimal acoustic complex media with near-arbitrary targeted functionalities. The scheme is generally applicable beyond acoustics, with broad implications to other wave types. Our results demonstrate unprecedented control over multiple-scattering waves and establish complex media as a viable route to modal control and operations on compact platforms, providing a new design paradigm for multimode, reconfigurable wave-based devices with potential applications in multiplexed communication, imaging, and the manipulation of quantum waves.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to design reflectionless complex media with arbitrary unitary transmission matrices, experimentally demonstrating non-Abelian braiding of acoustic modes.
motivation: Full control of the transmission matrix in complex media is challenging; the authors aim to achieve this to enable arbitrary wave operations.
method: They use a multi-scattering approach and generalized Wigner-Smith operators to design optimal acoustic complex media for targeted unitary transmissions.
result: They experimentally demonstrated non-Abelian braiding of waveguide modes and showed that the principle extends to arbitrary unitary operations.
conclusion: The scheme offers a new design paradigm for multimode, reconfigurable wave-based devices, with potential applications in communications, imaging, and quantum wave manipulation.

title: On The Relation Between Perspective-neutral, Algebraic, And Effective Quantum Reference Frames
authors: Julian de Vuyst, Philipp A. Hoehn, And Artur Tsobanjan
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2196 (2026).

The framework of internal quantum reference frames (QRFs) constitutes a universal toolset for dealing with symmetries in quantum theory and has led to new revelations in quantum gravity, gauge theories and foundational physics. Multiple approaches have emerged, sometimes differing in scope and the way symmetries are implemented, raising the question as to their relation. Here, we investigate the relation between three approaches to QRFs for gauge symmetries, namely the [MATH] semiclassical, [MATH], and [MATH] (PN) approaches. Rather than constructing Hilbert spaces, as the PN approach, the effective approach is based on a quantum phase space parametrized by expectation values and fluctuations, while the emphasis of the algebraic approach is on the state space of complex linear functionals on a kinematical algebra. Nevertheless, external frame information is treated as gauge in all three formalisms, manifested in constraints on states and algebra. We show that these three approaches are, in fact, equivalent for ideal QRFs, distinguished by sharp orientations, which is the previous setting of the first two approaches. Our demonstration pertains to single constraints, including relativistic ones, and encompasses QRF changes. In particular, the QRF transformations of the PN framework agree semiclassically with those of the older effective approach, by which it was inspired. As a physical application, we explore the QRF covariance of uncertainties and fluctuations, which turn out to be frame dependent. This is particularly well-suited for the effective and algebraic approaches, for which these quantities form a natural basis. Finally, we pave the way towards extending these two approaches to non-ideal QRFs by studying the projection and gauge-fixing operations of the Page-Wootters formalism, built into the PN framework, on algebraic states.

.
tldr: This paper demonstrates the equivalence of three approaches to quantum reference frames for ideal gauge symmetries and explores the frame dependence of uncertainties.
motivation: Multiple approaches to quantum reference frames exist, and their relation is unclear; the authors aim to clarify how they compare.
method: They compare the semiclassical (effective), algebraic, and perspective-neutral (PN) approaches, showing they are equivalent for ideal QRFs, and analyze QRF transformations and projection/gauge-fixing operations.
result: The three approaches are equivalent for ideal QRFs, with QRF transformations agreeing semiclassically; uncertainties and fluctuations are frame-dependent.
conclusion: The work unifies these frameworks and paves the way for extending to non-ideal QRFs.

title: A 57fe Mössbauer Spectroscopy Study Of Spin-lattice Dynamics And Magnetic Transitions In Hexagonal Multiferroic Lu0.5Sc0.5FeO3
authors: Shixin Hu, Jijun Xue, Xiaoying Wang, Yili Cao And Hua Pang
abstract: Hexagonal Lu0.5Sc0.5FeO3 is a promising multiferroic candidate, yet its spin-lattice coupling and magnetic ground state are still under active debate due to difficulties in resolving subtle structural and magnetic features. Here, we employ 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy, complemented by synchrotron x-ray diffraction and magnetization measurements, to probe the spin-lattice dynamics and magnetic transitions across 5–300 K. Our study reveals a cascade of spin-lattice dynamics: local FeO5 distortions emerge below TL = 180 K, followed by antiferromagnetic ordering at TN = 165 K and a spin-reorientation transition at TSR = 40 K, as anomalous multi-stage variations in effective lattice stiffness and vibrational response, accompanied by linewidth (LW) broadening in Mössbauer spectra. The magnetic ground state is unambiguously identified as a noncollinear configuration combining Γ1 and Γ2 irreducible representations, with subtle in-plane rotations of Fe3+ moments and weak out-of-plane ferromagnetism—a detail that Mössbauer spectroscopy uniquely resolves beyond the limitations of neutron diffraction. Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya (DM) interactions drive this noncollinearity, inducing a negative c-axis polarization via strong spin-orbit-lattice coupling. These results highlight the unique capability of Mössbauer spectroscopy in resolving delicate noncollinear magnetic structures and provide a unified picture for understanding spin-lattice entanglement in frustrated hexagonal multiferroics.
tldr: This paper uses Mössbauer spectroscopy to study spin-lattice dynamics and magnetic transitions in hexagonal Lu0.5Sc0.5FeO3, revealing noncollinear magnetic ordering and DM interaction-induced ferroelectricity.
motivation: The material is a promising multiferroic, but its spin-lattice coupling and magnetic ground state are debated. The authors aim to resolve these using Mössbauer spectroscopy, which can detect subtle magnetic structures.
method: They performed 57Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy combined with synchrotron X-ray diffraction and magnetization measurements over 5-300 K.
result: They identified a cascade of spin-lattice dynamics: local FeO5 distortions below 180 K, antiferromagnetic ordering at 165 K, and spin-reorientation at 40 K. The magnetic ground state is noncollinear with Γ1 and Γ2 representations, with weak out-of-plane ferromagnetism.
conclusion: DM interactions drive noncollinearity and induce negative c-axis polarization via strong spin-orbit-lattice coupling. The study demonstrates Mössbauer spectroscopy's capability in resolving noncollinear magnetic structures.

title: Probing Quark Electromagnetic Properties Via Entangled Quark Pairs In Fragmentation Hadrons At Lepton Colliders
authors: Qing-Hong Cao, Guanghui Li, Xin-Kai Wen And Bin Yan
abstract: Electromagnetic dipole interactions of light quarks induce distinct spin correlations in quark pairs produced at lepton colliders, favoring entangled spin-triplet state aligned along the axis or spin-singlet state. These correlations lead to unique azimuthal asymmetries in inclusive -dihadron pair production and in back-to-back hadron pairs ( ), which are absent in the SM. Using published Belle and BaBar measurements together with projected sensitivities based on ratios of azimuthal asymmetries, we demonstrate that these measurements provide significant constraints on light-quark dipole couplings, with a reduced dependence on poorly known nonperturbative fragmentation functions and free from contamination by other new physics effects. This approach offers a clean and novel probe of light-quark dipole interactions in collider experiments.
tldr: This paper proposes using spin correlations in entangled quark pairs produced at lepton colliders to probe light-quark electromagnetic dipole couplings, leveraging azimuthal asymmetries in dihadron production.
motivation: The Standard Model predicts negligible spin correlations for light quarks, whereas new physics dipole interactions would induce distinct spin-singlet or triplet correlations, offering a clean probe of such couplings.
method: The authors derive azimuthal asymmetries in inclusive and back-to-back dihadron production from quark spin correlations, and use published Belle/BaBar data and projected sensitivities to constrain dipole couplings, minimizing dependence on fragmentation functions.
result: The analysis shows that these measurements can provide significant constraints on light-quark dipole couplings, with reduced theoretical uncertainties from fragmentation and no contamination from other new physics effects.
conclusion: This approach offers a novel and clean collider probe of quark dipole interactions, but it is primarily a high-energy physics phenomenology study rather than a contribution to quantum information or quantum technologies.

title: El Agente Cuántico: Automating Quantum Simulations
authors: Ignacio Gustin, Luis Mantilla Calderón, Juan B Pérez-Sánchez, Chris Crebolder, Jérôme F Gonthier, Mohammad Ghazi Vakili, Yuma Nakamura, Karthik Panicker, Manav Ramprasad, Aiwei Yin, Zijian Zhang, Yunheng Zou, Varinia Bernales And Alán Aspuru-Guzik
abstract: Quantum simulation is central to understanding and designing quantum systems across physics and chemistry. However, its practical use is often limited by the exponential growth of Hilbert space and by the increasing complexity of modern quantum-simulation software. Here we introduce El Agente Cuántico, a multi-agent AI system that automates quantum-simulation workflows by translating natural-language scientific intent into executed and validated computations across heterogeneous quantum-software frameworks. By reasoning directly over library documentation and APIs, our agentic system dynamically assembles end-to-end simulations spanning—but not limited to—state preparation, closed- and open-system dynamics, tensor-network methods, quantum control, quantum error correction, and quantum resource estimation. The developed system unifies traditionally distinct simulation paradigms behind a single natural-language interface. Beyond reducing technical barriers, this approach opens a path toward scalable, adaptive, and increasingly autonomous quantum simulation, enabling faster exploration of physical models, rapid hypothesis testing, and closer integration between theory, simulation, and emerging quantum hardware.
tldr: El Agente Cuántico is a multi-agent AI system that automates quantum simulation workflows via natural language, unifying diverse quantum software frameworks.
motivation: Quantum simulation is hindered by the exponential growth of Hilbert space and the complexity of heterogeneous quantum software, limiting practical use.
method: The system uses AI agents that reason over library documentation and APIs to dynamically assemble end-to-end quantum simulations from natural-language intents.
result: It unifies simulation paradigms (state preparation, dynamics, tensor networks, control, error correction, resource estimation) behind a single interface, reducing technical barriers.
conclusion: This approach enables scalable, adaptive, and increasingly autonomous quantum simulation, accelerating hypothesis testing and integration with quantum hardware.

title: Promise Of Graph Sparsification And Decomposition For Noise Reduction In Qaoa: Analysis For Trapped-Ion Compilations
authors: Jai Moondra, Phillip C. Lotshaw, Greg Mohler, And Swati Gupta
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2185 (2026).

We develop new approximate compilation schemes that significantly reduce the expense of compiling the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) for solving the Max-Cut problem. Our main focus is on compilation with trapped-ion simulators using Pauli-[MATH] operations and all-to-all Ising Hamiltonian [MATH] evolution generated by Molmer-Sorensen or optical dipole force interactions, though some of our results also apply to standard gate-based compilations. Our results are based on principles of graph sparsification and decomposition; the former reduces the number of edges in a graph while maintaining its cut structure, while the latter breaks a weighted graph into a small number of unweighted graphs. Though these techniques have been used as heuristics in various hybrid quantum algorithms, there have been no guarantees on their performance, to the best of our knowledge. This work provides the first provable guarantees using sparsification and decomposition to improve quantum noise resilience and reduce quantum circuit complexity. For quantum hardware that uses edge-by-edge QAOA compilations, sparsification leads to a direct reduction in circuit complexity. For trapped-ion quantum simulators implementing all-to-all [MATH] pulses, we show that for a [MATH] factor loss in the Max-Cut approximation ([MATH], our compilations improve the (worst-case) number of [MATH] pulses from [MATH] to [MATH] and the (worst-case) number of Pauli-[MATH] bit flips from [MATH] to [MATH] for [MATH]-node graphs. This is an asymptotic improvement for any constant [MATH]. We demonstrate that significant improvements to the approximation ratio are obtained using decomposition in simulated trapped-ion experiments with dephasing noise. We further present a generic argument showing that sparsification results in an exponentially improved circuit fidelity lower bound in digital computing schemes based on one- and two-qubit gates, which are relevant to a wide variety of hardwares such as superconducting qubits and certain neutral atom or trapped ion setups, and more sophisticated noise models. We anticipate these approximate compilation techniques will be useful tools in a variety of future quantum computing experiments.

.
tldr: The paper develops approximate compilation schemes for QAOA using graph sparsification and decomposition to reduce circuit complexity and improve noise resilience in trapped-ion simulators.
motivation: Existing QAOA compilations are expensive and noise-sensitive; the authors aim to reduce circuit depth and improve fidelity.
method: They apply graph sparsification (reducing edges while preserving cut structure) and graph decomposition (splitting weighted graphs into unweighted ones) to derive compiled circuits with provable guarantees.
result: They achieve asymptotic reductions in pulse count and Pauli-X flips for trapped-ion implementations, and show improved circuit fidelity lower bounds for digital gates.
conclusion: These techniques offer practical approximate compilation methods for near-term quantum devices, but are not aligned with the user's specific research directions.

title: New Physics Opportunities At Neutrino Facilities: Bsm Physics At Accelerator, Atmospheric, And Reactor Neutrino Experiments
authors: Koun Choi, Doojin Kim, Jong-Chul Park, Seodong Shin, Pouya Bakhti, Ki-Young Choi, Chang Hyon Ha, Kazumi Hata, Wooyoung Jang, Yu Seon Jeong, Young Ju Ko, Hyun Su Lee, Weijun Li, Yu-Feng Li, Mehedi Masud, Kenny C Y Ng, Jungsic Park, Min-Gwa Park, Komninos-John Plows, Meshkat Rajaee, Eunil Won, Byeongsu Yang, Seong Moon Yoo, Jaehoon Yu And Seokhoon Yun
abstract: Since the discovery of the Higgs boson, the long-standing task at hand in particle physics is the search for new physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM), which accounts for only about 5% of the Universe. In light of this situation, the neutrino sector has drawn significant attention due to neutrino oscillations, which require physics BSM and have prompted a wide array of active and planned experimental programs. Notably, neutrino facilities offer substantial potential to search for new physics beyond neutrino oscillations, owing to their precision measurement capabilities, diverse experimental configurations, and various neutrino sources. This white paper summarizes the landscape of new physics that can be probed at current and future neutrino experiments, categorized into laboratory-produced and cosmogenic signals. We discuss recent experimental results interpreted through the lens of new physics, as well as detailed plans and projected sensitivities of next-generation facilities. This summary is based on presentations from the 4th Workshop on New Physics Opportunities in Neutrino Facilities, the 4th Workshop on New Physics Opportunities at Neutrino Facilities (NPN 2024), held at Institute for Basic Science in Daejeon, Korea, on 3–5, June 2024. Particular emphasis is placed on accelerator-based neutrino experiments and a range of neutrino programs in East Asia. We also outline key tasks necessary to realize the promising new physics opportunities ahead.
tldr: This white paper summarizes the landscape of new physics beyond the Standard Model that can be probed at current and future neutrino facilities, covering accelerator, atmospheric, and reactor experiments.
motivation: The search for new physics beyond the Standard Model, particularly in the neutrino sector, which requires BSM physics due to neutrino oscillations.

abstract: This review systematically summarizes the principles, technological advancements, and diverse applications of Stokes-vector and Mueller-matrix polarization imaging (PI). While traditional polarimetry is limited to point-by-point measurements, PI captures the polarization state in a two-dimensional scene, generating a spatial map of parameters for complex and heterogeneous systems. The Stokes–Mueller formalism is the only complete mathematical tool for polarization analysis, using the Stokes vector to describe the light’s state and the Mueller matrix as the transfer function to fully characterize the polarization-altering properties of any medium, including complex depolarizing tissues. The evolution of PI from time-sequential to snapshot paradigms represents a pivotal shift, driven by the pressing need for real-time, motion-artifact-free characterization of dynamic systems. While time-sequential systems laid the foundational framework, their inherent trade-off between acquisition speed and polarization completeness has spurred intense innovation in snapshot methodologies. This transition is not merely a technical improvement but a fundamental enabler for applying polarization analysis to in vivo biological processes and real-time industrial inspection. Applications of PI are wide-ranging, including label-free diagnostics for cancer detection, non-destructive analysis of anisotropic materials, polarization-enhanced target detection, and so on. A future direction is the convergence of PI with hyperspectral detection to form ‘hyper-Stokes/Mueller imaging,’ which promises unprecedented specificity and real-time capability.

title: The Paradox Of Steady-state Light Diffusion
authors: André Liemert, Lorenzo Pattelli, Alwin Kienle, Federico Tommasi And Fabrizio Martelli
abstract: For over thirty years, the definition of the diffusion coefficient in light transport has been the subject of persistent debate. Its canonical expression includes an explicit dependence on absorption, violating a fundamental scaling property of the radiative transfer equation (RTE). In the time domain (TD), evidence shows that the correct definition is independent of absorption, yet absorption-dependent formulations unfortunately remain common in practical data analysis. In the continuous-wave regime, the radial decay of the RTE can be reproduced by an absorption-dependent coefficient, but this does not imply that steady-state transport is genuinely diffusive. Here, this controversy is resolved through an exact consistency test based solely on the requirement that diffusion converges to the RTE in the limit of infinite propagation. In the TD, we prove that the absorption-independent coefficient is both necessary and sufficient for exact long-time convergence. In the continuous-wave regime, we prove analytically that no scalar diffusion coefficient can make diffusion asymptotically equivalent to the RTE when absorption is nonzero: matching the dominant attenuation length fixes one coefficient, whereas matching the residue requires a different one. We further show that this failure is not caused by any finite set of ballistic or few-scattering contributions, and quantify the intrinsic error introduced by incorrect parameterizations in idealized absorption-retrieval scenarios. These results establish the time-domain formulation as the only self-consistent reference and call for a re-examination of how diffusion is applied in optical transport studies.

conclusion: The time-domain formulation is established as the only self-consistent reference for diffusion in optical transport, calling for re-examination of how diffusion is applied in studies with absorption.
